key_insight: A convolutional Kolmogorov-Arnold network (KATO) can optimize ship structures directly for forced-vibration performance using active input power, while keeping designs connected and manufacturable.
engineering_relevance: This enables lighter, feature-size-controlled ship deck and foundation designs that better resist machinery-induced vibration, noise, fatigue, and resonance-related failure.
method: Active input power (AIP) as the vibration objective
Helmholtz PDE filtering + Heaviside projection for manufacturability
evidence_signal: Across deck and frame cases, KATO reduced AIP versus size-optimized or GCMMA references, matched GCMMA within 0.5 dB in tested frame variants, and was 6.4-10.4x faster in stress-aware formulations.
watch_item: The strongest gains depend on proper handling of resonance, filtering, and post-optimization binary re-analysis, so implementation details may affect real-world performance.
paper_title: Neural topology optimization of ship structures under propulsion machinery vibrations
